tests.mutation: GroundspeedLimit.Knots printed 88 knots (`Groundspeed.InKnots(88m)` for `InKnots(87m)`); this test went red. It went red too with GroundspeedLimit.Authority citing operating-limitations' `§ 107.51 introductory text` instead of speed-limit's locator.

Speed.Limit never took the one-figure branch (`asOneFigureIn is { } unit && unit == (SpeedUnit)99`), so a request for one figure resolved to the limit as printed instead of declining; this test went red for both units.

Waivers.Suspension ignored the statement (`return false ? ... : null` for `return statement.InForce ? ...`), so a stated waiver was not honoured and the limit resolved; this test went red. It went red too with the decline citing waiver-policy's `§ 107.200` instead of waivable-regulations' `§ 107.205`.
Handlers.SpeedLimit defaulted a missing statement to none held (`request.Waiver ?? WaiverStatement.NoneHeld(Speed.Regulation, "the engine")` for `Demand(request.Waiver, ...)`); this test went red.

Waivers.Suspension compared the statement's regulation with itself (`statement.Regulation, statement.Regulation` for `statement.Regulation, regulation`), so a waiver of § 107.41 suspended § 107.51(a); this test went red.

Groundspeed.Exceeds counted equality as exceeding (`>=` for `>`), so 100 mph was beyond the 100 mph figure and declined; this test went red. It went red too with GroundspeedFinding.Authority citing `§ 107.51` rather than the entry's `§ 107.51(a)`.

Speed.Within reported every comparable groundspeed within the limit (`new GroundspeedFinding(groundspeed, true, limit)` for `!beyondKnots`); this test went red. It went red too with the knots figure printed as 88.

Speed.Within let the knots figure govern (`beyondKnots == beyondKnots` for `beyondKnots == beyondMilesPerHour`), so 87 knots and 100.01 mph resolved within the limit instead of declining; this test went red. It went red too with the miles-per-hour figure governing, and with the decline citing operating-limitations' `§ 107.51 introductory text`. Citing speed-within-limit's own locator did NOT turn it red: both entries cite `§ 107.51(a)`, so the locator cannot tell them apart and only Attempted names speed-limit.

Speed.Within skipped its own gate check (`is { } suspended && suspended.Reason == UnresolvedReason.UnsupportedRule`), so the decline came from speed-limit's gate and named speed-limit rather than speed-within-limit; this test went red. It went red too with Waivers.Suspension ignoring the statement (`return false ? ...`).

Waivers.Suspension treated every statement as a waiver in force (`return true ? ...` for `return statement.InForce ? ...`), so a statement that none is held still declined OutsideCurrentScope; this test went red.

Handlers.SpeedWithinLimit defaulted a missing statement to none held (`request.Waiver ?? WaiverStatement.NoneHeld(Speed.Regulation, "the engine")` for `Demand(request.Waiver, ...)`); this test went red.
